Network Comparison Test

Source: R/nct.R
nct.Rd

nct() tests whether two networks estimated from two samples of the same variables differ, at the three levels of van Borkulo et al. (2022): network structure (statistic M, the largest absolute edge difference), global strength (statistic S, the difference in the summed absolute edge weights, or with abs = FALSE in the summed signed weights, the global expected influence) and individual edges (statistic E, the absolute difference of each edge). Each network is an EBIC graphical lasso network of the Pearson correlations, and each p-value comes from re-estimating both networks on permuted group labels (within-pair swaps with paired = TRUE).

A p-value counts the permutations whose statistic is at least the observed one, with the observed split added: (sum(perm >= observed) + 1) / (iter + 1), so the smallest attainable value is 1 / (iter + 1). A non-significant test does not show that the networks are equal; with small samples the test has little power (van Borkulo et al. 2022). The edge tests are many tests at once; set p_adjust before reading single edges. Both networks are regularised estimates, so check how stable each one is with boot_glasso().

Usage

nct(
  data1,
  data2,
  iter = 1000L,
  gamma = 0.5,
  paired = FALSE,
  abs = TRUE,
  weighted = TRUE,
  p_adjust = "none",
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise")
)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
print(x, n = Inf, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

data1

The observations of group 1: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per observation. Non-numeric columns are dropped; at least two numeric variables and three rows are needed.

data2

The observations of group 2, with the same variables as data1 in the same order; columns that differ in name or order raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input. An unnamed matrix is matched by position and takes the other group's names, or V1, V2, ... when neither group has names.

iter

The number of permutations, a whole number of at least 1. Default 1000.

gamma

The EBIC tuning parameter of the glasso, a non-negative number; larger values give sparser networks. Default 0.5.

paired

Whether row i of both groups is the same unit (such as a person measured twice). Each permutation then swaps the two rows of a unit at random instead of shuffling all rows, and the groups need the same number of rows, otherwise an error of class nestimate_bad_input is raised. Default FALSE.

abs

Whether global strength sums the absolute edge weights. With FALSE, it sums the signed weights (global expected influence). Default TRUE.

weighted

Whether the tests compare the weighted networks. With FALSE, both networks are binarised (an edge is present or absent) before the statistics are computed. Default TRUE.

p_adjust

The multiplicity correction for the per-edge p-values, any method of stats::p.adjust(). Default "none".

na_method

How missing values are handled. "pairwise" (default) keeps every row, permutes rows as usual, and estimates each sample or permuted split from its pairwise-complete correlation matrix, with the median pairwise co-observation count as the sample size; a variable pair sharing fewer than two observed rows there raises an error of class nestimate_degenerate_sample. "listwise" drops incomplete rows first (with paired = TRUE, a pair is dropped when either member is incomplete). Complete data are unaffected by the choice.

x

For the print() and as.data.frame() methods: a net_nct object.

n

For the print() method: the number of edges to list, largest difference first. Default Inf (all).

...

For the print(), summary() and as.data.frame() methods: ignored.

object

For the summary() method: a net_nct object.

row.names, optional

For the as.data.frame() method: ignored, kept for compatibility with the base generic.

Value

A net_nct object. print() reports the three tests, each group's global strength and the edges, largest difference first, and returns the object invisibly; summary() returns the M and S tests as a data frame with one row per test. The object's fields:

nw1, nw2

The estimated weighted adjacency matrices of the two groups (binarised with weighted = FALSE).

structure

The network-structure test (statistic M, the largest absolute edge difference): observed, perm (the statistic in each permutation) and p_value.

strength

The global-strength test (statistic S): the same, plus by_group, each network's global strength (NCT's glstrinv.sep).

E

The per-edge tests: observed and p_value hold one value per node pair (the upper triangle), perm is an iter by node-pair matrix, and edge_names is a data frame with the columns from and to naming each node pair.

n_iter

The number of permutations.

groups

The display names of the two groups: the argument names when they are plain variables, otherwise "group 1" and "group 2".

n

The rows used in each group.

paired

Whether a paired test was used.

params

The settings used: gamma, abs, weighted, p_adjust and na_method.

The letters follow van Borkulo et al. (2022) and NetworkComparisonTest. Before Nestimate 0.9.27 the fields M and S held the global-strength and network-structure tests the other way round; reading them now raises an error of class nestimate_renamed.

For the summary() method: a data frame with one row per global test and the columns test ("network structure", and "global strength", or "global expected influence" when abs = FALSE), statistic ("M", "S"), observed, p_value and significant (p_value < 0.05, a fixed level). The as.data.frame() method gives one row per node pair, with the columns from, to, weight_1 and weight_2 (the edge in each group's network), difference (statistic E), p_value and significant (p_value < 0.05).

Details

nct() follows NetworkComparisonTest::NCT() with its defaults abs = TRUE, weighted = TRUE and paired = FALSE. The network estimator is EBIC-selected glasso (psychnets::ebic_glasso()) applied to a Pearson correlation matrix made positive definite with Matrix::nearPD() (NCT's NCT_estimator_GGM default). Under the same seed both functions permute the same rows, so the permutation p-values agree; the glasso solver is not the Fortran one NCT wraps, so the test statistics agree to independent-solver precision (of the order of 1e-4) rather than bit for bit. The Matrix package (in Suggests) must be installed.

The two groups must hold the same variables in the same order; non-numeric columns, such as an id or a group label, are dropped first. Infinite values are refused; use finite observations or NA for missing data.

A variable without variation in a group, or in a permuted split (a rare binary item can be constant in a split), enters that network as an isolated node. The statistic is then defined on every split, so the permutation test stays exact. A constant variable in an observed group raises a warning of class nestimate_constant_variable.

Malformed iter, gamma, paired, abs, weighted or data raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

References

van Borkulo, C. D., van Bork, R., Boschloo, L., Kossakowski, J. J., Tio, P., Schoevers, R. A., Borsboom, D., & Waldorp, L. J. (2022). Comparing network structures on three aspects: A permutation test. Psychological Methods. doi:10.1037/met0000476

Examples

set.seed(1)
x1 <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 4), 100, 4)
x2 <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 4), 100, 4)
colnames(x1) <- colnames(x2) <- paste0("V", 1:4)
# iter = 20 keeps the example fast; a real analysis uses 1000 or more.
res <- nct(x1, x2, iter = 20)
res
#> Network Comparison Test: x1 vs x2
#> 20 permutations, independent groups, n = 100 and 100
#> 
#>   Test                  Statistic       p
#>   M  network structure      0.000   1.000 
#>   S  global strength        0.000   1.000 
#>        x1 0.000 vs x2 0.000
#>   E  edges differing       0 of 6
#> 
#>   Edges, largest difference first
#>   Edge         x1      x2  |diff|       p
#>   V1 - V2   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V1 - V3   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V1 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V2 - V3   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V2 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V3 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#> 
#>   * p < 0.05
summary(res)
#>                test statistic observed p_value significant
#> 1 network structure         M        0       1       FALSE
#> 2   global strength         S        0       1       FALSE
